h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ט Pesach — Maamar Lamed Tes

p: תּוֹרֵי זָהָב נַעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ עִם נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף
"Rows of gold we will make for you, with studs of silver"
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א', י"א).
(Shir HaShirim 1:11).
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
In the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א', נ"ה):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:55):
"תּוֹרֵי זָהָב" — זוֹ בִּיזַּת הַיָּם, "עִם נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף" — זוֹ בִּיזַּת מִצְרַיִם; כְּשֵׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין כֶּסֶף לְזָהָב, כֵּן יֵשׁ שֶׁבַח מָמוֹן הַיָּם מִבִּיזַּת מִצְרָיִם.

"'Rows of gold'—this is the spoils of the Sea; 'with studs of silver'—this is the spoils of Egypt; just as there is a difference between silver and gold, so is the wealth of the Sea superior to the spoils of Egypt."
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין: כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב
Now one must understand: since it is written
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, ל"ו):
(Shemos 12:36):
וַיְנַצְּלוּ אֶת מִצְרָיִם,
"And they emptied out Egypt,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּדָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגָן, כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים
which they expounded as meaning they left Egypt like a granary trap without grain and like sea-depths without fish
(בְּרָכוֹת ט':),
(Berachos 9b),
אֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּיזַּת הַיָּם גְּדוֹלָה מִבִּיזַּת מִצְרַיִם?!
how is it possible that the spoils of the Sea were greater than the spoils of Egypt?!
וּבֶאֱמֶת מַה שֶּׁבִּישְּׂרוּ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל, לֹא הָיָה הַכַּוָּונָה עַל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב,
In truth, what our father Avraham, peace be upon him, was promised—"And afterward they shall go out with great wealth"—did not refer primarily to silver and gold,
דְּאֵין מַעְצוֹר לַה' לִיתֵּן לָהֶם כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב מִבְּלִי שֶׁיִּקְחוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם;
for nothing prevents Hashem from giving them silver and gold without needing to take it from Egypt;
גַּם אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה חֲשִׁיבוּת אֶצְלוֹ כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאָמַר עַל הַפָּסוּק

moreover, to our father Avraham, peace be upon him, silver and gold held no importance, as I heard from our holy master [the Rebbe of Kotzk/Izhbitz], may the memory of the righteous and holy be for a blessing, who said on the verse
(בְּרֵאשִׁית י"ג, ב'):
(Bereishis 13:2):
וְאַבְרָהָם כָּבֵד מְאֹד בַּמִּקְנֶה בַּכֶּסֶף וּבַזָּהָב
"And Avraham was very heavy (kaveid) with livestock, with silver, and with gold"

שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה עָלָיו לְמַשָּׂא כָּבֵד הַקִּנְיָנִים וְהַכֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁלּוֹ, שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ הָיָה אַהֲבָה וְהָיָה יָרֵא שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס בְּלִבּוֹ חֶמְדָּה מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהָיוּ הַנְּכָסִים כְּבֵדִים עָלָיו!

that to our father Avraham, peace be upon him, his possessions, silver, and gold felt like a heavy burden, because his attribute was pure love of God and he feared lest any desire for worldly matters enter his heart, so his wealth weighed heavily upon him!
רַק עִנְיַן "וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל" הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁיּוֹצִיאוּ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִשָּׁם:
Rather, the essence of "And afterward they shall go out with great wealth" refers to the holiness they would extract from there:

וְאָז הָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם בְּגָלוּת הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁלְּעוּמַּת זֶה הָיָה אָז חָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוֹצִיאוּ הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוּשׁוֹת מִשָּׁם וְזֶה הָיָה אֶצְלָם הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְעַל זֶה נִתְבַּשֵּׂר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל.

for at that time the Torah was in exile in Egypt—manifesting externally as the "wisdom of Egypt"—and Israel extracted the holy sparks from there as a preparation for the Giving of the Torah, and it was of this that our father Avraham, peace be upon him, received the tidings, "And afterward they shall go out with great wealth."
רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּצְרְכוּ לִיקַּח כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב—שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
As for why they had to take physical silver and gold: in truth, everything the Holy One, blessed is He, created is for the sake of the righteous person, as they said
(בְּרָכוֹת ו':):
(Berachos 6b):
כָּל הָעוֹלָם לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה
"The entire world was created solely for this person"
וּקְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת גַּם בְּקִנְיָנִים שֶׁלּוֹ.
so his holiness extends into his possessions as well.
וְאִיתָא
And it is stated
(חוּלִּין צ"א.)
(Chullin 91a)
בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר עַל פַּכִּין קְטַנִּים:
regarding our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, who remained behind [alone at the Jabbok crossing] for small jugs:
מִכָּאן לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁמָּמוֹנָם חָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָן, וְכָל כָּךְ לָמָּה? לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם בְּגָזֵל.
"From here we learn that to the righteous, their money is dearer to them than their own bodies; and why so? Because they never stretch out their hands in robbery."
וְהוּא פֶּלֶא: וְכִי זֶהוּ טַעַם מַסְפִּיק לְהִסְתַּכֵּן עֲבוּר פַּכִּין קְטַנִּים?! וְגַם לְשׁוֹן "שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין" אֵינוֹ מוּבָן!
Now this is astonishing: is that a sufficient reason to endanger one's life for small jugs?! And also the phrase "they do not stretch out" is unclear!
וּכְהַאי לִישָּׁנָא אִיתָא גַּם כֵּן
And this exact same phrasing is also found
(סַנְהֶדְרִין צ"ט:)
(Sanhedrin 99b)
גַּבֵּי רְאוּבֵן: מִכָּאן לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם בְּגָזֵל
regarding Reuven [who took only ownerless mandrakes]: "From here we learn that the righteous do not stretch out their hands in robbery"
וְהוּא פֶּלֶא יוֹתֵר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִימּוּד עַל זֶה שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים אֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם בְּגָזֵל!
which is even more astonishing, that a scriptural proof is needed to teach that righteous people do not commit robbery!
פְּשִׁיטָא דְּמִי שֶׁגּוֹזֵל נִקְרָא רָשָׁע, שֶׁבֶּן נֹחַ גַּם כֵּן מְצֻוֶּוה עַל הַגָּזֵל, כְּעֵין קוּשְׁיַת הַגְּמָרָא
Obviously anyone who steals is called wicked, since even a descendant of Noach is commanded against robbery—just like the Gemara's question
(יְבָמוֹת כ'.):
(Yevamos 20a):
וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, "קָדוֹשׁ" הוּא דְּלָא מִיקְרֵי, "רָשָׁע" נַמִּי לָא מִיקְרֵי?!
"And is anyone who fails to uphold the words of the Torah merely not called 'holy'—is he not called 'wicked' too?!"
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר: מִכָּאן לִרְאוּבֵן שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק!
so it should have said, "From here we learn that Reuven was righteous"!

אַךְ שָׁם יִתָּכֵן שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי שֶׁרְאוּבֵן הָיָה עוֹד נַעַר קָטָן וְלֹא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵאִיסּוּר גָּזֵל, וְרַק הָיָה: רַגְלֵי חֲסִידָיו יִשְׁמֹר, וְאֵיבְרֵיהֶם לֹא יָכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ

However, there [regarding Reuven] it can be explained that because Reuven was still a young child and knew nothing at all of the prohibition of robbery, yet "He guards the feet of His pious ones" so their very limbs were incapable of doing anything against the will of Hashem, may He be blessed
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ רַבִּי מְנַחֵם מֶנְדֶּל מֵרִימָנוֹב זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל הַפָּסוּק
along the lines of what our holy master Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Rymanov, may the memory of the righteous be a blessing for the life of the World to Come, said on the verse
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ב, י'):
(Bereishis 22:10):
וַיִּשְׁלַח אַבְרָהָם אֶת יָדוֹ וַיִּקַּח אֶת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת
"And Avraham stretched out his hand and took the slaughtering knife"

מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁעָשָׂה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַד לְקִיחַת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת, שֶׁהָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, עָשׂוּ אֵיבְרֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֵעַצְמָם, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּלְקִיחַת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת לִשְׁחוֹט שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיָה זֶה רְצוֹן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, לֹא רָצוּ אֵיבָרָיו וְיָדָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת, רַק שֶׁשָּׁלַח אֶת יָדוֹ בְּכֹחַ מִמַּה שֶּׁחָשַׁד לְעַצְמוֹ פֶּן הוּא עָצֵל מִפְּנֵי אַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ

for all the actions our father Avraham, peace be upon him, performed up until taking the knife—which were truly the will of Hashem, may He be blessed—his limbs performed effortlessly on their own, whereas when taking the knife to slaughter Yitzchak, which was not actually Hashem's ultimate will, his limbs and hands refused to move, so he had to force his hand out because he suspected himself of laziness out of love for his son

וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: מִכָּאן לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם בְּגָזֵל, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּדֵיהֶם בְּעַצְמָן אֵינָם רוֹצִים לִפְשׁוֹט יָד בְּגָזֵל, וְדִיֵּיק זֶה מֵרְאוּבֵן שֶׁהָיָה עוֹד נַעַר קָטָן וּבְלִי דַּעַת נִשְׁמַר מֵעַצְמוֹ מִגָּזֵל וְלֹא לָקַח רַק מִן הַהֶפְקֵר.

and this is what they meant by "From here we learn that the righteous do not stretch out their hands in robbery," meaning their very hands refuse to stretch out for stolen property, which is inferred from Reuven who was still a young boy without legal awareness and yet instinctively refrained from theft, taking only ownerless produce.

וְכָאן שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים מָמוֹנָם חָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָן לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶן בְּגָזֵל, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לוֹקְחִים מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מַגִּיעַ לָהֶם מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר

And here [regarding Yaakov], when it says that to the righteous their money is dearer than their bodies because they do not stretch out their hands in robbery, it means they never take anything not allotted to them by Hashem, may He be blessed, along the lines of what is said
(Mishlei 30:8):
לֶחֶם חֻקִּי
"My allotted portion of bread"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁנֶּחְקַק וְנִקְצַב מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְחֶלְקוֹ, וְקָרֵי לֵיהּ גָּזֵל עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
meaning that which was engraved and apportioned by Hashem, may He be blessed, as one's specific share, whereas anything beyond that is called "robbery," as they said
(בְּרָכוֹת ל"ה:):
(Berachos 35b):
כְּאִילּוּ גּוֹזֵל לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
"[One who enjoys this world without a blessing] is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed is He, and Knesses Yisrael"
כִּי לַה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ, וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִילָם הוּא אֶצְלָם כְּגָזֵל וְאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם לִיקַּח;
for "The earth is Hashem's and the fullness thereof," so whatever was not created specifically for them is to them like robbery and they refuse to take it;
וּמִפְּנֵי זֶה מָמוֹנָם שֶׁמְּיוּחָד לָהֶם, שֶׁנִּבְרָא בִּשְׁבִילָם, חָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁמָּסַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם

and therefore their own possessions, which are uniquely designated for them and created for their soul's sake, are so precious to them that our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, risked his life for them

עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁסִּיפֵּר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁשָּׁמַע מֵרַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי בּוּנָם מִפְּשִׁיסְחָא זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאָמַר בְּשֵׁם הַיְּהוּדִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁדָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לַצַּדִּיק מְחוּיָּיב לֵיהָנוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ אַף בִּמְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ.

along the lines of what our holy master recounted having heard from our master Rabbi Bunim of Peshischa, who said in the name of the Holy Yehudi, may their righteous and holy memories be for a blessing, that an object belonging to a righteous person's soul-root he is obligated to utilize and elevate even with self-sacrifice.
וְלָכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁהַפַּכִּים קְטַנִּים הֵם שֶׁלּוֹ וְשַׁיָּיכִים לְנַפְשׁוֹ וְנִבְרְאוּ בִּשְׁבִילוֹ, מָסַר נַפְשׁוֹ לְהַעֲבִירָם;
Therefore our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, knowing that those small jugs belonged to him, were connected to his soul, and were created for him, risked his life to bring them across;
וְכֵן עִנְיַן כָּל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם הָיָה מַה שֶּׁרָצוּ לְהוֹצִיא הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁהָיָה כְּבוּשָׁה בְּתוֹכָם.
and likewise the entire purpose of all the silver and gold they took out of Egypt was to extract the holiness that was trapped within them.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Arizal, Shaar HaMitzvos, Mishpatim — “Every soul comprises many sparks of the lights; according to its lights is the bounty bestowed on it from above, and according to that bounty is the money he has in this world. So one who steals from him steals the supernal bounty descending to his soul; even if it is worth only a perutah, he robs a perutah's worth from his soul. Thereby you will understand why Yaakov went back for small jugs: his money is drawn to him from the supernal bounty bestowed on his soul, and if he is not sparing of it, he disdains that bounty; and if he abandons a lost perutah, that perutah of bounty is lost above as well.” Connection: The Arizal gives the Kabbalistic root of Rav Tzadok's point that a tzaddik's possessions belong to his soul: wealth is the measure of the soul's own sparks, so Yaakov's small jugs were part of himself.

p: וּמָצִינוּ אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אַף שֶׁהָיָה מִדָּתוֹ אַהֲבָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן עֲשִׂירִי כְּתִיב
Now we find regarding our father Avraham, peace be upon him, that even though his primary attribute was love, nevertheless after the tenth trial [the Akeidah] it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ב, י"ב):
(Bereishis 22:12):
עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אָתָּה
"Now I know that you are a God-fearing man"
וְאַף שֶׁלְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הָיָה זֶה מֵרוֹב אַהֲבָתוֹ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁדָּחָה אַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ יְחִידוֹ, אַךְ שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה הִיא הַיִּרְאָה עִילָּאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ

for even though outwardly it appeared to stem from his overwhelming love of Hashem, may He be blessed, overriding his love for his only son, yet the perfection of love is Supernal Awe (Yirah Ila'ah), as they said in the Midrash
(שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים קי"ב):
(Shocher Tov, Tehillim 112):
כַּמָּה עָשָׂה אַבְרָהָם וְלֹא נִתְהַלֵּל אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה יָרֵא לְפָנָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר
"How much Avraham did, yet he was praised only for fearing before Him, as it is said, 'For now I know, etc.'"
וְהַיְינוּ יִרְאָה עִילָּאָה: יְרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה
which is Supernal Awe—"I feared out of my very joy," as they said in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah
(Chapter 3).

וְכֵן יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם, אָז הוֹצִיאוּ הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוּשׁוֹת מִמִּדַּת חֶסֶד וְאַהֲבָה וַעֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּדָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגָן, דְּהַיְינוּ קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וְכִמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים, הַיְינוּ הַחַיִּים בְּעַצְמָהּ, שֶׁבְּדָגִים נִזְכַּר בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה "נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" בַּתּוֹרָה.

And so too at the Exodus from Egypt, which was in the merit of Avraham, they extracted the holy sparks from the attribute of Chessed and love, leaving Egypt "like a granary trap without grain"—meaning sustenance of life—and "like sea-depths without fish"—meaning life itself, for regarding fish the term "living soul" (nefesh chayah) is first mentioned in the Torah.
וּבִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף כְּתִיב
Then at the Splitting of the Sea it is written
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, ל"א):
(Shemos 14:31):
וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה
"And Israel saw the Great Hand"
וְיָד הַגְּדוֹלָה הַיְינוּ יָמִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and "the Great Hand" refers to the right hand, as it is said
(דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א' כ"ט, י"א):
(I Divrei HaYamim 29:11):
לְךָ ה' הַגְּדֻלָּה,
"Yours, Hashem, is the greatness (Gedulah)"
הַיְינוּ מִדַּת חֶסֶד.
which is the attribute of Chessed.
וְהוּא שֶׁאָז הָיָה חֶסֶד גַּם לְמִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
That is, at that moment there was kindness even toward the Egyptians, as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ז:):
דַּאֲפִילּוּ הָכָא דִּינָא בְּרַחֲמֵי וְכוּלֵּי וְאִתְקְבָרוּ בְּאַרְעָא וְכוּלֵּי, הֲדָא הוּא דִּכְתִיב: נָטִיתָ יְמִינְךָ תִּבְלָעֵמוֹ אָרֶץ
"That even here judgment was tempered with mercy, etc., and they were buried in the earth, etc., as it is written, 'You stretched out Your right hand, the earth swallowed them'"
וְהוּא דְּמַה שֶּׁפְּלָטָן הַיָּם חַיִּים יֵשׁ טַעַם בַּמְּכִילְתָּא
for regarding the sea casting them onto the shore while still alive, one reason in the Mechilta
(Beshalach 6)
מִפְּנֵי הַבִּיזָּה, וְיֵשׁ טַעַם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאוּ הַמִּצְרִים וְיִתְקַיֵּים בָּהֶם: אַךְ תֵּרֶא אֹיַבְתִּי תְּכַסֶּהָ בוּשָׁה
is for the sake of the spoils, and another reason is so that the Egyptians would see and there would be fulfilled in them "Then my enemy shall see, and shame shall cover her"

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז הַמִּצְרִים שֶׁפְּלָטָן הַיָּם וְרָאוּ מַה הִגִּיעַ לָהֶם וְרָאוּ הַנִּסִּים הִכִּירוּ אָז הָאֱמֶת לְשָׁעָה וְנִתְקַיֵּים בָּהֶם: וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי ה', וְזֶה חֶסֶד גָּדוֹל לָהֶם שֶׁהִכִּירוּ הָאֱמֶת;

meaning that the Egyptians whom the sea cast up alive saw what had befallen them and witnessed the miracles, thereby recognizing the truth for a moment and fulfilling "And Egypt shall know that I am Hashem"—which was a great kindness to them, that they recognized the truth;
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁפַּרְעֹה הִקְרִיב, וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
and likewise because Pharaoh "drew near," as stated in Midrash Rabbah
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ה')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:5)
שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁעָשׂוּ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה גַּם כֵּן לְהַכִּיר אַחַר כָּךְ הָאֱמֶת, וְזֶה הוֹעִיל לְמִצְרַיִם שֶׁזָּכוּ לִקְבוּרָה,
that he drew Israel near to the repentance they performed, and through this he too merited afterward to recognize the truth, which benefited the Egyptians so they merited burial
וְזֶה: וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה ה' בְּמִצְרַיִם, דְּהַיְינוּ הַחֶסֶד שֶׁפְּלָטָן הַיָּם חַיִּים וְהִכִּירוּ הָאֱמֶת לְפִי שָׁעָה.
and this is "And Israel saw the Great Hand that Hashem wrought upon Egypt," namely the kindness of casting them ashore alive so they recognized the truth temporarily.
וּכְתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ: וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת ה', וְלֹא כְּתִיב "וַיִּירְאוּ אוֹתוֹ"
And immediately afterward it is written: "And the people feared Hashem," and not "and they feared Him"
וְהַיְינוּ הֲוָיָ"ה מַלְכָּא עִילָּאָה, דְּהִיא יִרְאָה עִילָּאָה: יְרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי;
which refers to Havayah, the Supernal King, representing Supernal Awe—"I feared out of my very joy"

וְאָז הוֹצִיאוּ כָּל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִמִּצְרַיִם: שֶׁבַּתְּחִילָּה הוֹצִיאוּ אַךְ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְזֶה מְכוּנֶּה בְּשֵׁם "נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף", וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַיָּם זָכוּ לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶם אַף הַקְּדוּשָּׁה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא,

and then they extracted all the holiness from Egypt: for initially [in Egypt] they extracted only the holiness of the Written Torah, termed "studs of silver," whereas afterward at the Sea they merited to extract from them even the holiness of the Oral Torah, which emanates from the Dew of Atika,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(אִיּוֹב כ"ח, י'):
כָּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ
"His eye saw every precious thing"
רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכוּלֵּי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
the eye of Rabbi Akiva, etc., saw, as they said in the Midrash
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה י"ט, ו' וּבְתַנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת ו')
(Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6 and Tanchuma Chukas 6)
וְאָז הָיָה נִכְלָל כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְזֶה זָכוּ בְּבִיזַּת הַיָּם.
and then the entire Oral Torah was encompassed within the Written Torah, which they merited through the spoils of the Sea.
וְנִקְרָא בִּיזַּת הַיָּם "תּוֹרֵי זָהָב", דְּזָהָב מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכְּתִיב: וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת ה', וְהַיְינוּ מַלְכָּא עִילָּאָה כָּאָמוּר
And the spoils of the Sea are called "rows of gold," because gold signifies awe, since it is written "And the people feared Hashem," referring to the Supernal King as stated
(בְּמַאֲמָר הַקּוֹדֵם),
(in the previous Maamar),
שֶׁאָז זָכוּ לִנְהוֹרָא דְּעַתִּיקָא;
for then they merited the light of Atika;
וּבִיזַּת מִצְרַיִם נִקְרָא "נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף", שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל אַהֲבָה, שֶׁאָז הוֹצִיאוּ רַק הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהִיא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת אַהֲבָה.
whereas the spoils of Egypt are called "studs of silver," which signifies love, because then they extracted only the holiness of the Written Torah, which comes through the attribute of love.
וְזֶה שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' נ"ג:):
לֹא תֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עַד עוֹלָם — עַד דְּיִתְּעַר הַאי עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי; כְּדֵין כְּתִיב: וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר—הֲדָא הוּא דִּכְתִיב: מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעוֹלָם דַּיְיקָא,

"'You shall see them no more until eternity (ad olam)'—until that supernal world awakens, etc.; then it is written, 'And Israel saw Egypt [dead upon the seashore], etc.'—this is what is written, 'from the world and unto the world (ad ha'olam)' specifically"

וְהַיְינוּ עָלְמָא עִילָּאָה, וְאָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה שֶׁלֹּא תּוֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עַד זְמַן זֶה שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְעָלְמָא עִילָּאָה, וְ"עַד הָעוֹלָם" דַּיְיקָא, דְּהוּא קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁאָז רָאוּ אוֹתָם וְהוֹצִיאוּ מֵהֶם הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוּשׁוֹת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,

which refers to the Supernal World (Binah/Atika), for Moshe told them they would see them no more until that moment when they would merit the Supernal World—specifically "until that World," which was at the Splitting of the Sea when they saw them and extracted the holy sparks from them in full perfection,
וְזֶהוּ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן;
which is the holiness of the Oral Torah emanating from the Dew of Atika, the primordial light;
כְּדֵין כְּתִיב: וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ
and immediately then it is written, "And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant," as we explained
(לְעֵיל),
(above),
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל אֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה: עֵינַי בְּנֶאֶמְנֵי אֶרֶץ, שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַדַּעַת לָשֶׁבֶת עִמָּדִי
which signifies surpassing faith—"My eyes are upon the faithful of the land"—the attribute of Da'as "to sit with Me"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ל"ז).
(as explained in Maamar 37).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 52 — “And this is ‘rows of gold we will make for you’—this is the spoils of the Sea, for then they merited supernal fear, as it is said ‘and the people feared,’ which is all of man’s effort: ‘What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear.’ ‘With studs of silver’ is the spoils of Egypt, which came from the side of kindness and through it they merited love, but only for the moment; therefore the studs of silver are like a point. And this fear is likened to gold, which is the completion of love that comes through fear, just as Avraham Avinu was completed in his attribute of love through his surpassing fear at the Akeidah.” Connection: Continues this maamar’s gold-and-silver reading; it adds that the love from Egypt was only momentary, “a point,” and that fear is man’s own effort, through which love is then given.

Once handed over, then it is written, 'And Israel saw Egypt dead on the shore of the sea.' This is 'from the world (olam) to the world' — 'to the world,' precisely. Then: 'And they believed in Hashem.'"
